transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Sam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SRE); Daniel (FinEdge Head of ML), Aisha (FinEdge Platform), Ravi (CTO)

Summary: weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning. Reviewed 2-day run results, spotted tail-latency on bursty workloads, discussed increasing concurrency and enabling continuous batching and prefix caching. Agreed to run longer steady-state test with production-like traffic and to validate queueing/backpressure behavior on Dedicated tier.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes, main goals are run review and config next steps
00:18 Daniel: thanks, quick note we had some infra flakiness earlier but cleared it out, so the numbers I sent overnight should be clean-ish, there might be a small spike at 2pm sample that I didn't scrub
00:34 Sam: great, I pulled the run from yesterday - two nodes, nv4a-ish, sorry the auto transcript calls them N V 4 a - we ran the continuous batching prototype with kv cache enabled, batching window 12ms, target concurrency 60 across the pool
00:50 Aisha: can you remind us which model variant was used? we need that to map costs
01:03 Sam: we used redwood-rebel-13b-v2 (the lighter quantized variant) — again apologies if transcript shows "redwood rebel" weirdly; quantization profile Q4_0 with some custom kernels on the runtime
01:20 Ravi: we measured avg throughput 310 reqs/s, but p95 latency drifted to ~450ms on bursts, so cost looks OK but latency spikes are concerning
01:40 Sam: yes that's consistent, when request shape is bursty our batching window increases effective batch size which improves amortized GPU compute but adds queuing latency. The tradeoff is continuous batching buys token efficiency but hurts tail latency if concurrency not tuned
02:05 Maya: could you explain how KV cache hit ratio impacted this run? earlier we thought it would reduce tokens and improve perf
02:20 Sam: kv cache hit was ~28% on the test set; because many of FinEdge prompts are fairly unique prefixes, caching helps some but not as much as in chat-style workloads. Also we saw some "KV cash" misses - transcription shows that - where prefetching wasn't hitting due to slight prompt normalization differences
02:41 Daniel: yeah we noticed the normalization issue, our client sometimes has trailing spaces and different field order in JSON which likely breaks exact prefix matches
03:00 Priya: from infra side we saw GPU utilization swing 40-85% during bursts; autoscaler didn't kick because we pinned node count for the POC, that may also add to queueing
03:20 Sam: recommendation A: increase target concurrency to 90-100 at the same batching window so GPU stays fuller but queueing is spread — this should reduce p95 from 450ms to ~280-320ms based on our sim
03:41 Aisha: does that materially increase cost? our CFO asked about cost per 1M requests
03:52 Sam: small increase in active GPU hours but better token efficiency from larger effective batches usually offsets some cost; I'll produce a delta estimate. Full numbers depend on Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and whether preemption or burst capacity is used
04:12 Maya: recommendation B: tighten batching window from 12ms to 8ms during business-hours and keep 12-20ms in off-peak; that gives a better latency profile for 95th percentile
04:28 Daniel: can we do adaptive windows? e.g., lower window when queue depth exceeds threshold
04:38 Sam: yes runtime supports dynamic windowing heuristics; we can enable a heuristic that drops to 6-8ms when queued requests per-GPU > 40, otherwise relax to 15ms to favor cost
05:00 Aisha: curious about queueing/backpressure - when we increase concurrency are we risking client-side timeouts? our client times out at 1s
05:15 Maya: that's a good callout - we should correlate client timeouts with server queue times; one mitigation is to expose queue-depth metrics and to implement a 2-tier timeout where short timeouts fall back to a cheaper model/hosted endpoint
05:39 Sam: also there is a graceful-degrade path in the runtime: when queue exceed X we can route to small model variant or to cached responses. We'll demo that behavior next week
06:00 Ravi: show of hands, are we comfortable testing a Dedicated pool? we wanted to validate predictable throughput and to see if latency SLOs hold under steady-state
06:12 Daniel: yes we are open but need cost delta first
06:19 Maya: we'll prepare cost delta. For the Dedicated run we can pin 6 cards and run a steady 4-hour test to measure sustained throughput and variance
06:34 Sam: on the run we did yesterday, the effective batch sizes averaged 18 tokens per request and batch size per step 24 which gave good GPU efficiency. If we ramp concurrency to 95 we expect batch sizes to climb to mid-30s and utilize kernels better
06:56 Aisha: what about memory/kv cache pressure? if we increase concurrency will KV cache evictions rise and reduce hit rates?
07:09 Sam: yes could see more evictions; mitigation is to increase KV cache size on the runtime or pin hot prefixes. For Dedicated we can increase CPU/RAM per worker to hold more cache
07:28 Priya: ops note - we'll need SSH/K8s access pattern for the Dedicated smoke test and a short runway to configure IAM + SSO; FinEdge compliance requires SAML and audit logging
07:42 Maya: we've flagged SAML + SOC2 docs in the shared folder; I'll resend security pack
07:52 Daniel: quick nit: the spreadsheet has a column labeled "p50_ms" but sometimes it's p50_token_ms; can you align metrics naming so we know token vs request latency
08:05 Sam: noted, will update the CSV exporter; also attach raw per-step traces so you can see where token decode contributes vs kv lookups
08:20 Aisha: about experiments: can we try two configs side-by-side? one with higher concurrency + smaller window, another with lower concurrency + larger window, and compare cost/latency per-1M requests
08:36 Sam: yes we can run A/B on Dedicated pool with traffic split; need to shape traffic to simulate real percentiles though
08:50 Maya: I'll help coordinate the traffic shaping and share a runner script; Daniel please confirm traffic percentiles you want simulated
09:03 Daniel: let's do a 70/20/10 split of small/medium/large prompts and add a 5% spike scenario to test burst handling
09:15 Sam: perfect. I'll also instrument queue depth, batch size, kv hits, GPU util, p50/p95/p99 and token-level timing
09:29 Aisha: would love a short doc explaining the tuning knobs and recommended defaults for our workload - a one-pager for the platform team
09:40 Maya: we'll draft that one-pager with recommended concurrency, batching windows, and fallback behaviors; attach to the ticket
09:52 Ravi: anything blocking us from running the 4-hour steady-state test on Friday? we just need the runner script and the Dedicated pool config
10:03 Sam: no blockers from Redwood, just need the payload and traffic profile from FinEdge and confirm IAM access for the smoke test environment
10:15 Maya: OK let's recap next steps after a quick pause
10:28 [brief hold music and cross talk] 
10:45 Recap (Maya): action items - Sam run 4-hour steady-state test and upload results.csv (due Fri 2026-10-09); Aisha share prod-like payload and percentiles (due Thu 2026-10-08); Maya send Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta and security pack (due Wed 2026-10-07). Schedule follow-up next Tuesday 10/13 10am PT to review results and demo queueing behavior
11:15 Daniel: sounds good, appreciate the clear plan
11:25 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in calendar and Slack, bye
11:30 End

Notes: shared artifacts referenced - "throughput-run-1000s.csv" (uploaded to shared drive), "tuning-one-pager-draft.md" (to be created), pricing spreadsheet link (sheet:FinEdge-Pricing-Delta). Some transcript words mangled by auto-transcribe ("kv cash", "NV4A").
